newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean police detain 11 union members.
newsitem.headline: South Korean police detain 11 union members.

text.p: South Korean police detained 11 representatives of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions on Tuesday as they attempted to deliver a petition to President Kim Young-sam demanding that a controversial labour law be revoked.
"Twelve were detained by riot police, but one was immediately released," union official Min Dong-won said.
About 40 unionists had headed for a hot spring resort in the Northern Chungchong province where Kim is spending his New Year holidays.

The confederation is demanding the government withdraw a labour law pushed through parliament last week that gives companies the right to lay off employees, hire temporary workers and replace strikers.

The detained unionists were also petitioning that a law strengthening the powers of the Agency for National Security Planning, the Korean version of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency, be overturned, Min said.
The confederation said since strikes began on December 26, 49 union members have been detained. All but the most recent 11 unionists have been released.
